# apicp_firewall_rule (Resource)

Manages one rule in apicp's node-wide default-DROP firewall (PLAN.md §8 phase 7, requires `apicp_firewall` to actually be enabled for this to have any live effect). apicp refuses to create a drop/reject rule with no `source` restriction that would block SSH (22) or apicp's own control-plane API/agent ports (8080/8443) for everyone - the single mistake most likely to cause an unrecoverable lockout with no remote recovery path. To limit who can reach those ports use `apicp_firewall_restriction`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "apicp_firewall" "this" {}

# Allow one specific admin IP full SSH access even if a later rule
# below would otherwise restrict it - rules are evaluated in creation
# order, before the fixed baseline allow-list.
resource "apicp_firewall_rule" "admin_ssh" {
  depends_on = [apicp_firewall.this]
  source     = "203.0.113.50/32"
  port       = "22"
  protocol   = "tcp"
  action     = "accept"
  comment    = "office IP"
}

# Block a known-bad IP entirely.
resource "apicp_firewall_rule" "block_attacker" {
  depends_on = [apicp_firewall.this]
  source     = "198.51.100.23/32"
  protocol   = "all"
  action     = "drop"
  comment    = "repeated brute-force attempts"
}

# One rule for several sources, IPv4 and IPv6 mixed.
resource "apicp_firewall_rule" "block_scanners" {
  depends_on = [apicp_firewall.this]
  sources    = ["198.51.100.0/24", "203.0.113.77", "2001:db8:bad::/48"]
  protocol   = "all"
  action     = "drop"
  comment    = "scanner ranges"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `action` (String) `accept`, `drop`, or `reject`. Changing this replaces the resource.
- `protocol` (String) `tcp`, `udp`, or `all`. Changing this replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `comment` (String) Free-text note. Changing this replaces the resource (no update endpoint exists server-side).
- `port` (String) Single port (`"22"`) or inclusive range (`"1000:2000"`). Omit for all ports. Changing this replaces the resource.
- `source` (String) CIDR (v4 or v6) or bare IP this rule applies to. Omit for "anywhere" (`0.0.0.0/0`/`::/0`). Changing this replaces the resource.
- `sources` (Set of String) Further CIDRs or bare IPs (any mix of IPv4 and IPv6) this rule applies to, in addition to `source`. One rule covers all of them. With neither `source` nor `sources` the rule applies to anywhere. A drop/reject rule for SSH/8080/8443 is only accepted when every source is specific. Changing this replaces the resource.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
